data.content_ref: inline:The target's claim states the preference for falsificationism is defensible 'only if' one abandons 'the claim that this methodology tracks truth or probability.' Yet the target's own mechanism asserts the rule 'maximizes the speed of error detection.' Maximizing error-detection speed is itself a truth-tracking property: a rule that eliminates false theories faster than alternatives tracks truth (or at least tracks away from falsehood) better than those alternatives. The mechanism thus asserts an epistemic virtue that constitutes truth-tracking, directly contradicting the claim's necessary condition that truth-tracking must be abandoned. The target is internally inconsistent: it cannot simultaneously say the preference is defensible only if we stop claiming truth-tracking, and that the preference works by maximizing a truth-tracking metric (speed of error detection).
